research_question: What is the effect of mobile phone reminders sent to parents or caregivers, compared with routine immunisation care without reminders, on receipt of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/Penta-3) in children in low- and middle-income countries?
treatment_label: Mobile phone reminders (SMS text messages or phone calls)
outcome_description: Receipt of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3 / DPT3 / pentavalent-3 / Penta-3) at primary follow-up
positive_direction: A risk ratio greater than 1 (RR > 1) indicates a higher proportion of children receiving DTP3/Penta-3 in the mobile phone reminder arm compared with routine care (favours reminders)
search_queries: mobile phone SMS reminder child immunization pentavalent DTP trial
text message reminders caregiver childhood vaccination DPT3 LMIC randomized
automated phone call reminders infant immunisation Penta-3 controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials (individual or cluster) evaluating mobile phone reminders (SMS text messages or phone/voice calls) sent to parents/caregivers for routine childhood immunisation in low- and middle-income countries
Comparison against routine immunisation care without mobile phone reminders
Reporting quantitative data on the receipt or completion of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3 / DPT3 / Penta-3)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomized controlled trial (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, observational, quasi-experimental, or non-randomized studies are excluded)
No comparison between mobile phone reminders (SMS/calls alone) and a routine care (no-reminder) control group
No extractable quantitative outcome data for DTP3/Penta-3 completion (missing event counts or denominators per arm)
Studies conducted outside low- and middle-income countries, or studies focusing solely on other vaccines without DTP3/Penta-3 data
moderators_to_extract: Reminder modality (SMS text message vs automated interactive voice response vs direct phone call)
Trial design (individually randomised vs cluster-randomised trial)
World Bank income classification / country region
Timing of primary assessment (e.g., by 14-18 weeks vs 6 months vs 12 months of age)
Frequency and schedule of reminders (single reminder vs multiple reminders)
effect_size_note: Extract raw unadjusted event counts (children who received DTP3/Penta-3) and ITT denominators (all randomized/enrolled children) per arm. For multi-arm trials, extract the isolated reminder arm versus routine care control, excluding incentive or education-only co-intervention arms. Do not convert adjusted ORs or cluster-adjusted GEE estimates when raw counts are available.
